Best NDT inspection software: start with your workflow, not a feature list

The best NDT inspection software is the one that fits how your company actually wins, staffs, performs, reports and bills a job. Before you look at any vendor, write down that workflow on one page. Then score every product against it using the checklist below, and make every vendor prove it in a demo on your own report formats.

Most bad software purchases in the inspection industry happen the same way. An owner or QA manager sees a slick demo of a report being generated, signs up, and six months later discovers that certifications are still in a spreadsheet, calibration dates are still on a whiteboard, and the office is still retyping timesheets into an accounting package. The report looked great; the business did not change.

This buyer's guide is written for owners, operations managers and Level IIIs at NDT service companies in the USA and Canada, from five-technician shops to multi-branch contractors. It gives you a scorecard, the questions to ask in a demo, the implementation risks that catch people out, and an honest picture of the effort involved. It deliberately does not talk about price. Price only means something once you know what you are buying and how much work it will take to get running, and those are the things most buyers underestimate.

How to choose NDT software: the scorecard

To choose NDT software, score each option on eight areas: reporting, certifications, calibration, dispatch, commercial (quotes and invoices), field use, customization and integration. Weight them by where your company loses the most time or money today. A shop that loses sleep over audits weights certifications and calibration; a shop that loses cash weights quoting and invoicing.

AreaWhat good looks likeRed flag in a demo
ReportingSeparate report type per method, with method-specific fields and its own numberingOne generic form with a method dropdown
CertificationsScheme, level, method, expiry and vision tests per technician, with automatic status and alertsCertificates stored only as attachments
CalibrationInstruments by serial number with calibration records, certificate register and due-date alertsCalibration held in a separate spreadsheet
DispatchCrew and equipment assigned to jobs, double-booking blocked, calibration and cert warningsA shared calendar with no checks
CommercialQuotes with codes and methods, invoices by job/PO, timesheets feeding billingExport to accounting and retype
Field useOffline capture, photos, on-screen signatureRequires live signal
CustomizationYour templates, your fields, your workflow configured for youChange requests go on a public roadmap
IntegrationOpen API to your accounting system or client systemsCSV export only

Score each area as strong, adequate or missing. Any area marked missing that you rely on daily is a deal-breaker, no matter how good the rest looks.

Scoring the reporting module

Reporting is where most buyers start, so be strict about it. Ask to see a report for each method you perform, not just UT. A real NDT reporting module knows that an RT report needs source, technique, IQI type and placement; an MT report needs technique and particle type; a PT report needs method and developer; a PAUT report needs focal laws; and a UT thickness report needs readings organised by location and direction.

Check the workflow too. There should be a clear path from draft through review and approval to sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures and room for a third-party or authorized inspector. Check references: can you record work order, WPS, drawing, contract, procedure and standard on each report? Finally check output: can the report come out on your letterhead, and can it fill your biggest client's Excel format automatically?

For comparison, the Atlantis NDT Reports app has 17 report types (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday/coating and computed radiography), each with its own numbering sequence, versioned templates in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML, and a marine mode that merges class society, inspector and calibration certificates into one PDF. See the details on the NDT Reports app page.

Scoring technician certification tracking

Technician certification tracking software should tell you, without anyone opening a folder, who is certified for which method at which level, under which scheme, and when it expires. If a demo shows certificates only as uploaded PDFs, that is document storage, not tracking.

Look for structured fields: scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP and others), level, method, certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, OJT hours, training hours and exam results. Vision tests need the same treatment: near vision to Jaeger J1 or J2, colour perception, examiner and expiry. Status should be computed by the system, not typed by a person, and there should be warnings well ahead of expiry. The real test is whether the rest of the system uses this data. Does a timesheet warn you if the technician's certificate is invalid? Does dispatch?

For US companies working to a written practice under SNT-TC-1A or CP-189, and Canadian companies with technicians holding NRCan certification, this is what auditors check first. In the Atlantis ERP, certification status is computed as active, expiring soon (90 days), expired or revoked; warning tasks and configurable email alerts go out ahead of expiry; and timesheets warn when a certificate is not valid. The Certificates app also holds exam sheets and certificate templates per scheme.

Scoring calibration management

Calibration management software for NDT has to work at the level of individual instruments and probes, by serial number, because that is the level at which a client or auditor will ask the question. Which flaw detector was used on this report, and was it in calibration that day?

In a demo, ask to see an instrument record with its calibration history: provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, whether the lab is accredited, pass or fail, and the next due date. Ask to see a register of calibration certificates with valid, expiring and expired status. Then ask the important question: what happens when someone tries to send that instrument to a job after its due date? If the answer is nothing, the system is a filing cabinet.

Atlantis Asset Management tracks each instrument, probe and related item by serial number with lifecycle status, calibration records and a calibration certificate register with expiry alerts. Team Assignments warns when assigned equipment is out of calibration and blocks double-booking of the same serial number. Issue and return of equipment runs through supervisor and manager approval with condition recorded both ways, and there is a maintenance log for firmware updates, probe replacement and repairs.

Scoring crew dispatch and scheduling

Crew dispatch and scheduling software for NDT is about checks, not just calendars. Anyone can put names on a calendar. The value is in the system refusing to put the same technician on two sites on the same day, refusing to book the same instrument twice, and warning you before you send a Level II whose certificate lapsed last week.

Look for technician availability that accounts for leave, training, sickness and existing assignments, with overlaps blocked. Look for site details, mobilisation and demobilisation dates, and a simple dispatch status that the office and field both understand. Utilisation and next-available date per technician help the owner see capacity when a big turnaround request comes in.

Atlantis Team Assignments runs jobs through planned, dispatched, in field, submitted and closed, with site GPS coordinates, mobilisation dates, an availability calendar and calendar, kanban and list views. It shows utilisation and next available date per technician. The field app pulls jobs assigned to the technician and equipment issued to them, so the report starts linked to the right job.

Scoring NDT quoting and invoicing

NDT quoting and invoicing software should know what an inspection job looks like commercially: day rates and hourly rates, standby and travel, equipment charges, consumables, and client PO numbers that must appear on every invoice or it will not be paid. If you have to rebuild every invoice from timesheets in a separate accounting package, the software has not done its job.

Ask the vendor to walk a job from quote to invoice. The quote should carry job type, site, dates and applicable codes, with NDT service lines flagged by method. The client should be able to accept it online. The job's timesheets should record work type (inspection, travel, standby, setup), method, billable flag and rate multiplier, and should flow into the invoice. The invoice should carry job and PO numbers, site and cost centres, and split labour, equipment and consumables.

Atlantis Quotations and Invoicing do all of this, with a custom-branded quotation PDF and invoice layout, and a financial dashboard showing revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA and outstanding invoices over twelve months. Taxes for US states and Canadian provinces are configured during implementation. If you already use QuickBooks or NetSuite and want to keep it, the open REST API can connect to it, scoped per implementation. Ask us to demo a job from quote to invoice.

NDT inspection software for small companies

NDT inspection software for small companies has to be light enough to run without a dedicated administrator, but complete enough that the owner stops being the system. For a shop with five to twenty technicians, the priorities are usually: reports out the same day, no expired certificates on site, no out-of-calibration instruments on a job, and invoices out on time.

Small companies should be wary of two things. The first is enterprise suites built for large owner-operators: they are powerful, but they assume you have an IT team and months to configure them. The second is single-purpose reporting apps that look cheap and easy but leave certifications, calibration and billing where they were. Many small shops end up stitching three or four tools together and paying for all of them in admin time.

The Atlantis ERP solution was built with the small and mid-sized contractor in mind: affordable, accessible and fully customizable, and set up for you by a team led by an ASNT NDT Level III rather than handed over as a blank system. You can start with a subset of apps, typically reports, certificates and equipment, and add dispatch, quoting and invoicing when you are ready. Pricing is quote on request.

Demo questions to ask any NDT software vendor

Take this list into every demo and ask the vendor to show, not tell. If they cannot show it live, write it down as not proven.

  1. Show me an RT report with source, technique, IQI type and IQI placement, then a PAUT report with focal law data.
  2. Show me a UT report with the probe calibration captured inside it.
  3. Turn off the Wi-Fi on the tablet. Now finish a report, take a photo and sign it.
  4. Take a report through draft, review, approval and sent, including a third-party inspector signature.
  5. Fill my client's Excel template from report data without copying anything by hand.
  6. Add a technician whose MT Level II expires in 60 days. What does the system do today, and what happens on the day it expires?
  7. Log a vision test that expires next month. Who gets warned, and how?
  8. Assign a flaw detector whose calibration is overdue to a job. What happens?
  9. Try to put the same technician on two jobs on the same day.
  10. Build a quote with codes and methods, have it accepted, and turn it into an invoice with the client PO.
  11. Record timesheets with travel and standby, and show them on the invoice.
  12. Show me a procedure moving through review and approval, and its revision history.
  13. Change a field on a report template. Who does that, and how long does it take?
  14. Show me the API and tell me which systems you have connected it to.
  15. Who will set this up for us, and do they understand NDT?

Implementation risks and how to avoid them

The biggest risk in any NDT software rollout is not the software. It is data, habits and time. Plan for these risks up front and most rollouts go smoothly.

  • Dirty certification data. Expiry dates in old spreadsheets are often wrong or missing. Clean them before import, and have your Level III sign off the list, because the system will start warning on day one.
  • Unlabelled equipment. If serial numbers and calibration certificates are not matched today, the calibration register will expose it. Do a physical count first.
  • Template sprawl. Many contractors have several versions of the same report. Pick one per method (plus client-mandated formats) before templates are built.
  • Field resistance. Technicians who have used paper for years will push back. Start with one crew and one method, and let them shape the form.
  • Big-bang go-live. Switching everything on at once overloads a small office. Phase it: reports and certificates, then equipment and dispatch, then commercial.
  • No owner. Someone inside your company has to own the system. In small shops this is usually the QA manager or Level III.

Total effort: what the rollout asks of your team

Buyers usually ask about price first, but effort is what decides whether the rollout succeeds. In practice, the work falls into four stages.

Discovery. A few working sessions where the vendor learns your methods, report formats, certification schemes, equipment list, job flow and billing rules. Your Level III, office manager and a senior technician should all be in the room.

Data preparation. Your team gathers technician certificates and vision tests, the equipment list with serial numbers and calibration certificates, current procedures, and customer and rate information. This is the stage that depends most on you.

Configuration and templates. The vendor builds report templates, certificate templates, workflows and invoice layouts. You review and correct. With Atlantis, this is done by our team, and anything that is not a built-in feature is configured during implementation.

Pilot and rollout. One crew uses the field app on live jobs while the office runs the approval and invoicing side. Fix what they find, then roll out to the rest. After go-live, plan for a short period of support while habits settle. Ask us to scope an implementation plan for your company.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT inspection software for a small company?

The best option for a small company is one that covers reports, certifications and calibration in one place, works offline, and is set up for you rather than handed over blank. The Atlantis ERP solution is affordable, accessible and fully customizable, and can start with a few apps and grow.

How do I choose NDT software?

Write down your job workflow, score each option on reporting, certifications, calibration, dispatch, commercial, field use, customization and integration, and make every vendor prove each point live on your own formats. Any missing area you rely on daily is a deal-breaker.

What questions should I ask in an NDT software demo?

Ask the vendor to finish a report offline, show method-specific RT and PAUT fields, show what happens when a certificate or calibration expires, block a double booking, and take a job from quote to invoice. If it cannot be shown live, treat it as not proven.

How long does it take to implement NDT software?

It depends mostly on how clean your certification, equipment and template data is. A phased rollout, starting with reports and certificates, is faster and less disruptive than switching everything on at once. Atlantis scopes the plan with you before starting.

Can NDT software connect to QuickBooks or our client's systems?

The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and can connect to QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Maximo or any system that accepts API connections, with the scope agreed per implementation.

How much does NDT inspection software cost?

Atlantis does not publish prices because every setup is scoped to your methods, team and integrations. Pricing is quote on request through the contact page.
